title: Inference Prescriptor playbook - UI scribbles and backlog
body:
Context / purpose:
- Working doc for a compact UI that surfaces cost/perf prescriptions (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles) and lets engineers simulate + apply recommendations to routes/models.
- Not a final spec; intended as a mix of wireframe notes, acceptance criteria, and a groomed backlog for 2-sprint work.

Goals / user outcomes:
- Surface high-value recommendations with estimated token-cost delta, latency impact, and confidence score (quick triage).
- Enable safe 'dry-run' simulation for a route (est. savings vs. potential quality delta).
- Provide 1-click quick-apply presets and an advanced editor for rule tuning.
- Integrate with rollouts (canary/A-B) and Redwood Optimize telemetry so ops can monitor regressions.

Key UX components (sketch text):
1) Left rail: Filters + context
   - Time window (last 24h / 7d / 30d), traffic percentile selector (p50/p95/p99), model family dropdown, route tags.
   - Toggle: show only 'high confidence' recs.
2) Main list: Recommendation feed (compact cards)
   - Card header: "Prescript: <type>" (Batching / Cache / Quantize) + short label (e.g., "Batch: route /api/generate-chat")
   - Badge row: estimated token savings (e.g., "~12% tokens"), expected p95 latency delta ("+8ms" or "-22ms"), confidence (High/Med/Low).
   - Quick-actions: Inspect (open preview), Simulate, Apply -> Quick-apply (one of presets: safe, aggressive), Save as rule.
   - Inline micrograph: tiny sparkline for tokens/sec or cost trend.
3) Right panel: Recommendation inspector (expanded)
   - Simulation mode: input traffic slice, modulation of aggressiveness slider, preview of sample outputs (random prompt set) with diff highlights for potential quality regressions.
   - Safety checks: list of failing test prompts (from eval set), privacy flag if KMS/keys involved, required approvals for private deployments.
   - Deploy options: Apply (immediate), Canary (x% traffic for y hours), Draft rule (store in library).
4) Rule library: searchable list of saved prescriptions; show linked routes, owner, last used, enabled/disabled toggle.

Wireframe interaction notes (rough):
- Hovering a card shows a compact explainer: "why recommended" (e.g., "route uses short prompts -> good batching opportunity"), plus link to underlying metric query.
- Clicking Simulate runs a cost/latency model using sampled traces; show 95% CI and a small table of affected routes and estimated monthly $ delta.
- Quick-apply defaults for safety: small batch increments (e.g., increase batch size by 1, enable local prefix caching for <2s partials, use 4-bit quant profile for embeddings-only models).
- If quantization recommendation applied, show hardware compatibility matrix and fallback path (auto-unquantize on >error-rate).

Backlog & grooming (prioritized):
- P0: Recommendations feed backend + compact card UI (1 sprint). Deliverables: feed API, basic card, filters, quick-sim stub. Acceptance: feed displays top 50 recs, clicking Simulate shows delta numbers.
- P0: Simulation engine (approx cost + latency) with sample traces (two model families initially). Acceptance: sims within 15% of modeled lab results.
- P1: Inspector panel + sample-output diffs + eval-set checks (2 sprints).
- P1: Rule library CRUD + audit log + owner assignment.
- P2: Canary rollout integration with Console rollouts (coordinate with console team).
- P2: Advanced presets & templating (user-editable templates).
- P3: Per-tenant guardrails (enterprise: approval flows, max-allowed-quantization).
- Spike: Quantization safety monitoring (telemetry hooks to detect hallucination/regression signals) — 1 week spike.

Acceptance criteria (example for P0):
- UI shows recommendations grouped by type and route; each card displays token savings, latency impact, and confidence.
- Simulate returns a small results payload with cost delta and per-route estimate within target error.
- Quick-apply creates a draft rule in the library (not a live change).

Open questions / risks:
- How do we measure "quality delta" reliably for short prompts? Need to align on eval-set coverage and sampling jitter.
- Privacy/regulatory: quantization or caching recommendations may imply storing partial prefixes—do we surface a compliance flag automatically?
- Operator trust: how to present uncertainty so users don't blindly apply aggressive recs? Suggest confidence + required canary for low-confidence recs.
- Backend cost model accuracy: initial model will be conservative, might under-sell value.

Notes to engineering / infra (deferred design):
- Feed should be paginated cursor with scoring metadata (score = estimated monthly $ saved * confidence).
- Add a lightweight simulation lambda that replays sampled traces; cap replay size to avoid overload.
- Instrumentation: add telemetry events for 'recommendation_shown', 'simulate_clicked', 'apply_clicked', 'rule_created'.

Sketch of sample UI flow (user story):
- PM notices Route /api/chat has rising token cost. Opens Prescriptor tab -> sees a "Batch increase" card with ~9% token savings, med confidence. Clicks Inspect -> simulation shows output diffs for 5 evaluation prompts (no regressions). Chooses Canary 5% for 24h. Monitor shows cost drop and no eval alerts -> roll out to 100%.

Quick mental models (language for copy):
- "Prescriptions are recommendations to reduce inference unit cost while preserving output quality. Use Simulate to preview impact. Apply creates a rule that can be canaried and audited."

Design constraints and microcopy ideas:
- Badge naming: "Estimated token savings", "Expected latency change", "Confidence" (use color + tooltip).
- On low-confidence recs: use explicit warning: "Low confidence: run a canary and review sample outputs before applying to production routes."

Next steps / TODOs (owner assignments):
- Maya: prototype cards in Figma (due 2026-02-28) -> link to figma TBD.
- Jordan: spike on simulation accuracy with sample traces (due 2026-02-12).
- Priya: draft API contract for feed + apply endpoints (OPT-431) by 2026-02-19.
- Ethan: coordinate rollout integration with Console team (sync 2026-02-05).

Appendix: sample recommendation text (for copy):
- "Increase batch size for route /api/summary to 4. Expected: ~11% token-cost reduction, p95 latency +6ms, confidence: Medium. Rationale: average prompt length <120 tokens and steady traffic at 40r/s."

-- end --
